incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service=redwood-gpu-pool-A region=us-east-1 metric=cuda_alloc_fail_rate threshold=5% — 12 alerts in 5m. Auto-escalation to on-call

pagerduty: Incident PD-4521 created and routed to rotation oncall@redwood. Pager: alex (on-call)

alex (on-call): acked PD-4521 :white_check_mark: seeing noisy cuda alloc failures from pool-A metrics. digging in.

maya (on-call): pinging — I just pulled the grafana dashboard, GPU mem pressure spike across pool-A and pool-B between 15:02-15:06. Could be KV cache churn.

alex (on-call): logs from serving-runtime show repeated "CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY" in model-worker-762 and worker-880. Dumping pod logs now.

jay (eng-runtime): taking a look — if it's KV cache fragmentation we should see high kvcache eviction rate and large allocation attempts. Can you paste the tail of the worker logs?

alex (on-call): ```
I0315 15:03:12.123 serving_runtime.cc:452] Alloc(844M) failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
I0315 15:03:12.124 evictor.cc:89] KVCache evict 128MB shard=3
I0315 15:03:12.125 worker.cc:210] fallback to cpu backend triggered for request id=abc123
```

liz (sre-ops): note: autoshedder kicked in for some routes; traffic fallthrough to CPU pool observed. Customer-visible latency spike ~400-800ms for some requests. Sam — any customer reports?

sam (cs): no active high-sev tickets yet but a few users in enterprise-alpha mentioned timeouts in their /generate routes ~15:05. I'll flag them.

maya (on-call): plan: 1) isolate noisy nodes in pool-A, 2) drain pods to pool-C (smaller jobs), 3) temporarily reduce kvcache size config for pool-A via feature flag to avoid big allocs, 4) if still failing, scale up ephemeral GPU nodes. Agree?

jay (eng-runtime): +1. Quick mitigation steps: run `kubectl cordon <node>` on nodes with repeated OOMs, then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` to move pods. Also reduce `KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES` from 64GB to 16GB via configmap rollout for pool-A.

alex (on-call): executing cordon/drain on node gpu-a-12 (oom count 7), gpu-a-15 (oom count 4). Running: `kubectl cordon gpu-a-12 && kubectl drain gpu-a-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

incident-bot: :information_source: Action taken: node gpu-a-12 cordoned and drained at 15:12:03 by alex. Autoshedder prevented immediate mass evictions.

liz (sre-ops): after drains, observed decrease in cuda_alloc_fail_rate on pool-A from 7.2% -> 2.1% within 3m. Some residual failures on pool-B still showing.

jay (eng-runtime): I'm rolling out a temporary config patch to set KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=16GB in pool-A config. Patch applied via k8s rollout restart deployment/serving-runtime-pool-A.

maya (on-call): pushed the config, starting rollout 15:18. Monitoring for regressions.

alex (on-call): also toggled fallback policy to prefer model-variant-lowmem for larger seq lengths to avoid crazy allocations.

sam (cs): FYI notified enterprise-alpha about degraded perf, suggested workaround: reduce max_tokens in their requests until we confirm stability.

jay (eng-runtime): small note — logs show some CUDA driver warnings before OOM: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 79` which often indicates GPU memory corruption or fragmentation after long-running processes. We're patching runtime to recycle long-running processes > 8h.

alex (on-call): metrics look much better now. cuda_alloc_fail_rate pool-A 1.2%, pool-B 2.9%. Latency for routed CPU fallbacks dropping as load shifts back.

maya (on-call): PD-4521: moving from triggered -> acknowledged -> responder working. Flagging for follow-up postmortem to look at kvcache fragmentation and long-lived processes.

liz (sre-ops): agreed — action items: 1) postmortem to root cause kvcache eviction pattern; 2) autoshedder tuning to avoid cascading fallbacks; 3) longer-term: implement graceful process recycling per jay's note.

sam (cs): closing the loop with customer — will send status update summarizing mitigations and ask for logs if they still see issues.

alex (on-call): marking incident as mitigated at 15:28. Keeping PD incident open for RCA. Thanks all :heart:
